question.:question/problem: Given that $F=\left(3 \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\right)\,i+\left(- 3 \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}\right)\,j,$ what is $\text{div}\,F?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=\nabla\cdot F=\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}.
$$

When differentiating $P$ with respect to $x$, hold $y$ constant; when differentiating $Q$ with respect to $y$, hold $x$ constant.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla\cdot F & =\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial Q}{\partial y} \\  & =\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(3 \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}})+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(- 3 \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{3 x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}+\left(- \frac{3 y}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}\right) \\  & =\frac{3 \left(x - y\right)}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
